title: Isolation readiness decision ladder and comm lanes for private/VPC air-gapped requests
creator: Marina Patel
description:
Problem: Incoming private/VPC/on-prem customer requests often land as freeform forms or support threads. Network constraints (air-gapped controls, restrictive proxies, OS firewall rules, windows-only environments) are heterogeneous and require different engineering-level remediation and legal/compliance gating. Current intake is ad-hoc: we lose time clarifying requirements, escalate late, and surface incorrect SLAs to customers.

Goal: Create a short, prescriptive decision ladder (stepwise checklist + scoring) with clear communication lanes so PMs, Solutions, Sales, and Eng can triage requests within 48 hours and classify them into: Self-serve, Assisted onramp, Dedicated engineering runway, or Reject/Refer. The ladder must be implementable in the intake form and the handoff playbooks used by Solutions and SRE.

Deliverables: a) 1-page decision ladder doc, b) a 10-question network-readiness form and scoring implementation in Zendesk/Playbook, c) comms templates for each lane (customer-facing + internal), d) SLA expectations per lane, e) sample onboarding runbook for Assisted onramp lane.
acceptance_criteria: Decision ladder doc reviewed and approved by Eng, Security, and Solutions
10-question network-readiness form implemented in intake (Zendesk/Notion form) with scoring output
Handoff playbook created for Assisted onramp with explicit engineering tasks and timeboxes
Comms templates available for Self-serve, Assisted, Dedicated, and Reject lanes
Pilot of 12 live requests completes classification within 48 hours with feedback survey >= 4/5 from Solutions team
decision_rubric: Score 0-3 control plane connectivity: 0=isolated VPC, 3=public endpoint allowed
Thresholds: 0-4 = Self-serve with docs, 5-8 = Assisted onramp (Solutions + Eng 2 week runway), 9-12 = Dedicated engineering project (SLA contract), >12 = Reject / refer to partner
comms_plan: Self-serve: automated email + doc links; expected turnaround: immediate; assigned owner: Solutions (triage owner)
Assisted onramp: introduction email + 72h intake call scheduling; assigned owner: Solutions + Eng on call; expected runway: 2 weeks
Dedicated: commercial intake to SalesOps + contract scoping; expected runway: 4-12 weeks; notify Legal and Security
Reject/Refer: template explaining constraints and recommended 3rd-party partners or alternative architecture patterns
runbook_steps: Step 1: Customer submits intake form -> auto-score network readiness
Step 2: Automated triage routes to Solutions if score between 5-8 or to Sales if finance required
Step 3: Solutions leads a 30-min triage call within 48 hours to validate answers and gather artifacts (FW rules, proxy logs, appliance vendor docs)

Step 4: If Assisted lane, Solutions creates an engineering sub-issue with measured tasks: connectivity verification, minimal infra proof-of-concept, and security checklist completion (2 week estimate)
Step 5: If Dedicated lane, initiate contract playbook, assign Program Manager, schedule cross-functional kickoff and set milestones
Step 6: Track progress in intake dashboard and generate weekly sync to stakeholders until completion
notes: 2025-02-14 kickoff: PM + Solutions reviewed past 27 private requests; recurring blockers: outbound egress requirements, vendor support for non-Linux platforms, and corporate proxy certificates
Tradeoffs: more aggressive scoring reduces engineering load but risks false negatives; recommended conservative default with explicit override path
Ask from Security: include KMS/HSM exposure and data residency check as part of form
Implementation preference: first release as a Notion/Zendesk form + manual routing, followed by automation into Zendesk triggers in Q2
